newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria says rebel infighting results in massacres.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says rebel infighting results in massacres.

text.p: Algeria's President Liamine Zeroual on Tuesday told 10 political party leaders that violence was diminishing and blamed the latest wave of killings on rival Moslem rebel groups settling scores.

"President Zeroual...appeared very optimistic about the security situation," said one of the 10 officials, speaking to Reuters by telephone from Algiers. The meeting had been called to discuss preparations for planned parliamentary elections.
More than 300 people have died in the past four weeks -- coinciding with the Moslem feast of Ramadan -- in massacres and bomb attacks in Algiers and neighbouring hamlets and towns.
The authorities blamed Moslem rebels for the deaths.

About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.

The official, who did not want to be named, quoted Zaroual as saying: "The terrorism has died down recently compared to the past years. But the intensification of violent acts in the past weeks was confined and the massacres we had witnessed were settling of scores between opposed armed groups."
The authorities use the term terrorism to describe Moslem guerrilla factions trying to topple Zeroual's government.
The government plans to hold multiparty parliamentary elections later this year and Zeroual said the attacks were a reaction to this.
A bomb exploded on Monday in a schoolyard, wounding four 11-year-old boys near Algiers, an Algerian newspaper said on Tuesday.
